memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"If any member of the community sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD's commands, when they realise their guilt and the sin they have committed becomes known, they must bring as their offering for the sin they committed a female goat without defect."'" - Lev 4:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Finally, the ordinary Israelite. No title, no office, no authority. Just a member of the community.

And God gives him the same careful attention He gave the high priest. Same structure of instruction. Same requirement of a spotless animal. Same promise at the end.

Think about how unusual this was. In the ancient world, the sins of kings and priests mattered because kings and priests mattered. The sins of a farmer were nobody's concern. But the God of Israel wrote provision for the farmer into His law with the same care He wrote it for Aaron.

You matter to God. Not as part of a crowd, not as a statistic in a congregation, but personally. Jesus said the very hairs of your head are all numbered (Mtt 10:30). He told a parable about a shepherd leaving ninety-nine sheep to go after one (Lk 15:4).

There is a particular kind of loneliness in feeling spiritually unimportant — that God attends to the significant people and you are simply along for the ride. Leviticus 4 will not allow that thought. God devoted a section of His law to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever felt too ordinary for God to take a personal interest in me?
2. How does it change my prayers to know God attends to me individually?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You wrote provision for someone like me. Help me to believe that You know me by name and attend to me personally. Amen.
